5.0.s.en: 1. Bringing the holy things into the house

5.0.0.en: 1 Thus all the work that Solomon made for the house of the LORD was finished: and Solomon brought in all the things that David his father had dedicated; and the silver, and the gold, and all the instruments, put he among the treasures of the house of God.

5.0.1.en: Solomon was concerned to transfer the ark of the covenant from the city of David to the great house of the Lord that he had prepared, and he did not refer to the brass altar that Moses the prophet had set up in the wilderness; rather, a brass altar specific to the temple was set up.

5.0.2.en: The ark found its rest in the house of the Lord. The priests drew the staves out of the ark, so that the ends of the staves were seen from the ark, a sign that the journey of the wilderness had ended.

5.0.3.en: The ark of the covenant points to the Lord Christ, who dwelt among us by His Incarnation, that He might carry us over as to heaven, where our souls are settled and find rest in Him, while He is in us as His holy temple. By the saving work of Christ, He raised up from us a new earth and a new heaven in which His righteousness dwells in us.

5.0.4.en: Thus all the work that Solomon made for the house of the LORD was finished.

5.0.5.en: And Solomon brought in all the things that David his father had dedicated;

5.0.6.en: and the silver, and the gold, and all the instruments, put he among the treasures of the house of God. [1]

5.0.7.en: The book took every opportunity to point out that David had prepared all that was possible for the house of the Lord [1].

5.0.8.en: All the holy vessels, and also the silver and gold dedicated to the house, were placed in the treasuries of the temple, and there was no need for a celebration of bringing them into the treasuries, for it is the temple that sanctifies the gold, not the gold that sanctifies the temple (Mt 23:17).

5.0.9.en: Solomon took nothing of what his father had dedicated to the temple, or what the leaders or the people had given, or what had been placed in the palace treasuries for use in time of need.

5.1.s.en: 2. Bringing up the ark of the covenant into the house

5.1.0.en: 2 Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers of the children of Israel, unto Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD out of the city of David, which is Zion. 3 Wherefore all the men of Israel assembled themselves unto the king in the feast which was in the seventh month. 4 And all the elders of Israel came; and the Levites took up the ark. 5 And they brought up the ark, and the tabernacle of the congregation, and all the holy vessels that were in the tabernacle, these did the priests and the Levites bring up. 6 Also king Solomon, and all the congregation of Israel that were assembled unto him before the ark, sacrificed sheep and oxen, which could not be told nor numbered for multitude. 7 And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the LORD unto his place, to the oracle of the house, into the most holy place, even under the wings of the cherubims: 8 For the cherubims spread forth their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubims covered the ark and the staves thereof above. 9 And they drew out the staves of the ark, that the ends of the staves were seen from the ark before the oracle; but they were not seen without. And there it is unto this day. 10 There was nothing in the ark save the two tables which Moses put therein at Horeb, when the LORD made a covenant with the children of Israel, when they came out of Egypt.

5.1.1.en: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers of the children of Israel, unto Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD out of the city of David (which is Zion). [2]

5.1.2.en: It was fitting that the ark of the covenant be brought in with great reverence. True, new vessels were made for the temple, of large sizes suited to the size of the temple and the size of the service, which had grown far beyond what it had been in the tabernacle of the congregation. But the ark of the covenant, the mercy seat and the two cherubim upon the mercy seat all remained as they were, because the presence of God and His grace do not change however much the size of the temple building (or the church) changes, however much the number of those gathered for worship increases, and whatever the state of the Church may be in its material means. The Lord Christ affirmed that if two or three are gathered in His name, He is in the midst of them, as though they were two thousand or three thousand.

5.1.3.en: The ark of the covenant was brought in in the presence of a great multitude of the elders of Israel, who undoubtedly attended with reverence and in splendid array [2-4].

5.2.0.en: Wherefore all the men of Israel assembled themselves unto the king in the feast which was in the seventh month. [3]

5.2.1.en: This took place on the day of the feast with great joy, and they most probably counted this occasion a feast.

5.3.0.en: And all the elders of Israel came;

5.3.1.en: and the Levites took up the ark. [4]

5.4.0.en: And they brought up the ark, and the tabernacle of the congregation, and all the holy vessels that were in the tabernacle, these did the priests and the Levites bring up. [5]

5.4.1.en: They brought up with the ark also the tabernacle of the congregation with all the holy vessels that were in the tabernacle. These things were not set aside, because they had been sanctified to God; therefore they were neither changed nor beaten out to be used in making new vessels, and most probably some of them were not fit for use because of their smallness, so they were kept as a memorial.

5.4.2.en: Solomon brought up the holy vessels that David had prepared, together with the ark of the covenant and the tabernacle of the congregation, in a grand procession to the temple.

5.4.3.en: To prepare for this great procession Solomon gathered with the heads of the tribes and the heads of the fathers in the tent that David had prepared.

5.5.0.en: Also king Solomon, and all the congregation of Israel that were assembled unto him before the ark, sacrificed sheep and oxen, which could not be told nor numbered for multitude. [6]

5.6.0.en: And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the LORD unto his place, to the oracle of the house, into the most holy place, even under the wings of the cherubims: [7]

5.6.1.en: The Levites carried the ark of the covenant in the temple, but bringing it into the Holy of Holies was the work of the priests alone, since the Levites were not permitted to enter it.

5.7.0.en: For the cherubims spread forth their wings over the place of the ark,

5.7.1.en: and the cherubims covered the ark and the staves thereof above. [8]

5.8.0.en: And they drew out the staves of the ark, that the ends of the staves were seen from the ark before the oracle; but they were not seen without. And there it is unto this day. [9]

5.8.1.en: The staves were drawn out because the ark would not be moved afterward. Also, the drawing out of the staves points to rest, for our Lord Jesus rests in hearts that are open to Him as in His temple.

5.8.2.en: As we prepare a place for Him in our hearts, being His kingdom, He settles in them, and grants us also to settle in His heavenly Kingdom, which He prepares for us that we may settle in it.

5.8.3.en: The Lord longed for the ark of the covenant to settle in His holy temple, and the Apostle Paul says: “Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead)” (Rom 10:6-7).

5.8.4.en: “And there it is unto this day” does not mean the day on which the book was written, but the day on which the copy was written that was the source from which the writer copied, and they remained until the day of the destruction of Jerusalem (Ps 137:7).

5.9.0.en: There was nothing in the ark save the two tables which Moses put therein at Horeb, when the LORD made a covenant with the children of Israel, when they came out of Egypt. [10]

5.9.1.en: “There was nothing in the ark save the two tables which Moses put therein at Horeb” [10]. Aaron’s rod and the pot of manna were no longer in it.

5.10.s.en: 3. Offering the song of praise to God

5.10.0.en: 11 And it came to pass, when the priests were come out of the holy place: (for all the priests that were present were sanctified, and did not then wait by course: 12 Also the Levites which were the singers, all of them of Asaph, of Heman, of Jeduthun, with their sons and their brethren, being arrayed in white linen, having cymbals and psalteries and harps, stood at the east end of the altar, and with them an hundred and twenty priests sounding with trumpets:)

5.10.1.en: And it came to pass, when the priests were come out of the holy place:

5.10.2.en: (for all the priests that were present were sanctified, and did not then wait by course). [11]

5.10.3.en: The priests were sanctified when they came out of the Holy Place, for they had to come out so that the true King Himself might enter and proclaim His glory.

5.10.4.en: On that day not one course of the priests was present, but all the priests, for it was a general occasion that might not be repeated in the lifetime of the present generation of priests.

5.10.5.en: Sacrifices were offered, and it was fitting for all the priests to share in the celebration and to behold the glory of the Lord.

5.11.0.en: Also the Levites which were the singers, all of them:

5.11.1.en: of Asaph, of Heman, of Jeduthun, with their sons and their brethren, being arrayed in white linen, having cymbals and psalteries and harps, stood at the east end of the altar, and with them an hundred and twenty priests sounding with trumpets. [12]

5.11.2.en: The Church of the New Testament inherited from the temple the worship of praise, in which there were choirs of praise. It was said that the number of harps reached more than 4000 harps.

5.11.3.en: The Church, the daughter of Zion, imitates David the king and prophet, “the sweet psalmist of Israel” (2 Sam 23:1), for she has found in the Psalms new, joyful depths in the light of the work of the Son of David on the Cross, His Resurrection and His Ascension into heaven. The Apostle Paul defined the Kingdom of God as joy in the Lord (Rom 14:17).

5.11.4.en: v Whatever you do, do it well; by this you praise God[1].

5.11.5.en: v If even the angels, whose nature is simple and spiritual, are said to have tongues with which they sing hymns to their God and Creator, and offer Him thanksgivings without ceasing, how much more is it fitting for the spiritual bodies of men to do this after the resurrection, for all the members of the glorified body will have tongues in their mouths, giving voice to their speaking tongues, and so they will utter divine hymns overflowing with words of their love and their joys that fill their feelings[2].

5.11.6.en: St. Augustine v Praising God is a work proper to the angels.

5.11.7.en: v The Psalms give the soul tranquility and grant it peace, and calm in it the confusion of thoughts and the accumulation of desires... This book is the book of love... it is a weapon against Satan... it is a cause of rest after the toil of the day... it is the consolation of the aged... it is the source of our holy joys and sorrows... it is a wonderful hymn, it is the voice of the Church, it is incense of sweet fragrance[3].

5.11.8.en: v Hymns sung quietly in the mind bring one into a state of joy and calm.

5.11.9.en: St. Basil the Great v Who has the power, however great his experience, to enumerate the causes that stir the heart so that it is kindled and set ablaze with fire, and that urge it to devout prayers of great zeal? But we will mention a few examples of them...

5.11.10.en: Sometimes the singing of a passage of the Psalms stirs in us a fervent prayer.

5.11.11.en: And sometimes the harmony of the melody in the voice of one of the brethren rouses sluggish minds to many supplications.

5.11.12.en: Likewise the manner of utterance, together with the reverence of the one who chants (the praise), kindles zeal in those who are with him[4].

5.12.s.en: 4. The cloud, and the glory of the Lord fills the house

5.12.0.en: 13 It came even to pass, as the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the LORD; and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of musick, and praised the LORD, saying, For he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever: that then the house was filled with a cloud, even the house of the LORD; 14 So that the priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud: for the glory of the LORD had filled the house of God.

5.12.1.en: It came even to pass, as the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the LORD; and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of musick, and praised the LORD, saying, For he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever: that then the house was filled with a cloud, even the house of the LORD. [13]

5.12.2.en: This event is not mentioned in the Book of Kings.

5.12.3.en: The priests were sanctified, and came out of the Holy of Holies; then a hundred and twenty priests sounded with trumpets amid the praise of the choir, and the glory of the Lord came down like a cloud.

5.12.4.en: The priests stood in amazement as the cloud prevailed over them, and they became as those in heaven, and were filled with the fear of the Lord together with surpassing love for God.

5.12.5.en: The Lord proclaimed His glory in the temple: 1. Not when the animal sacrifices were offered, but when the sacrifice of praise and thanksgiving to God was offered, in which God delights (Ps 69:31). 2. When 120 priests joined in the praise with the choirs of singers from the three Levitical families. And the priests with all their trumpets stood at the east end of the altar [12], which is the nearest place to the people. 3. His glory was proclaimed when they celebrated the eternal mercies of God and His goodness, for the phrase “for his mercy endureth for ever” is repeated 26 times in (Psalm 136). The glory of God is proclaimed by His mercy and goodness.

5.12.6.en: The cloud of glory filled the temple and gave it a divine beauty, more beautiful than the gold that covered it, or the precious stones that adorned it; yet this glory cannot be compared with the glory that was to be revealed by the good news of the Gospel (2 Cor 3:8-10).

5.12.7.en: By the cloud that came down and filled the house of the Lord, the Lord proclaimed His acceptance of this temple, and that it was like the tabernacle of the congregation that Moses made, for by a cloud He declared His divine presence when Moses entered the tabernacle (Ex 40:34).

5.12.8.en: v May he who has died with Christ and risen with Him offer praise. May he pray toward the east. For this too is written in the Second Book of Chronicles, that after the house of the Lord was finished by King Solomon, on the very feast of the dedication the priests and Levites and singers stood toward the east, giving thanks to God, and praising Him with cymbals and harps[5].

5.13.0.en: So that the priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud: for the glory of the LORD had filled the house of God. [14]

5.13.1.en: The priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud, for the glory of the Lord filled the house of the Lord [14], and this is evidence that the Levitical priesthood would cease from service when the Messiah came, in whom all the fullness of the Godhead would dwell bodily, and when He comes to His temple, for He is like a refiner’s fire, and who may abide the day of His coming, and who shall stand when He appeareth (Mal 3:1-2).

5.13.2.en: God declared His appreciation of the weakness and inability of the priests who stood to serve Him, as they could not bear the brightness of His glory. What happened to the priests here happened to the disciples on Mount Tabor when they entered into the cloud (Lk 9:34).

5.13.3.en: Josephus describes what happened, saying: [Now as soon as the priests had put everything in its place with regard to the ark and had come out, a thick cloud came down and stood there, and spread gently through the temple. It was a moderate, spreading cloud, not a stormy cloud such as we see when rain falls in winter. The cloud darkened the place, so that no priest could distinguish another. But it gave the thoughts of all a visible and glorious picture of God’s descent into this temple, and His joyful dwelling inside His tabernacle.]

5.13.4.en: O Lord, rest in my heart!

5.13.5.en: v In Your humility, You gave Your people the ark of Your covenant, a sign of Your presence in their midst!

5.13.6.en: In the wilderness, whenever the ark moved they moved, and wherever it stopped they stopped.

5.13.7.en: And when Solomon built Your holy temple, the ark was placed in the Holy of Holies.

5.13.8.en: There the staves were drawn out of the ark, for it had settled at last in the Holy of Holies.

5.13.9.en: It settled where Your people settled in the Promised Land!

5.13.10.en: v Let Your presence be revealed within me.

5.13.11.en: As the ark settled in the Holy of Holies, and as You rested in the house of Mary and Martha and Lazarus, rest in my heart, and let me rest in You.

5.13.12.en: v You declared Your acceptance of the house that Solomon built, in whose building the leaders and the people and even some strangers shared, by the coming down of the cloud of Your glory in it.

5.13.13.en: No priest could see his brother priest, for Your surpassing mysteries drew all their hearts and their eyes.

5.13.14.en: v Let my tongue praise You together with my heart.

5.13.15.en: And let my depths rejoice in You, and offer You a new song of praise!
